description:
**[What the role is]**

We are looking for highly motivated and dynamic individuals to join our Regional Offices as Environmental Health Officers (EHOs). In this role, you will uphold high environmental public health standards and maintain clean, hygienic neighbourhoods through comprehensive inspections, investigation, enforcement, and stakeholder engagement to safeguard public health in Singapore.

**[What you will be working on]**

You will be responsible for the following:

You will conduct inspections across different premise types such as residential premises, dormitories, construction sites, commercial / trade premises, and public places to ensure integrated vector management and sanitation compliance. Your duties include performing vector surveillance, especially during outbreak of diseases such as dengue, identifying and addressing cleanliness and refuse management issues, investigating public feedback on environmental health matters, and conducting enforcement activities under the Environmental Public Health Act, Control of Vectors and Pesticide Act, and Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act. You will also engage directly with members of public, residents, premises owners, and stakeholders to promote environmental health best practices and vector prevention measures.

**[What we are looking for]**

The ideal candidate would possess the following qualities:

* Experience in environmental health operations, vector control, sanitation management, or related fields; professional certification in environmental health, vector control, or pest management will be advantageous.

* Strong analytical thinking and sound judgement for decision-making and investigations
* Good written and verbal communication skills for engaging diverse stakeholders and building positive relationships with community members
* A collaborative team player who works effectively with colleagues and supports team objectives
* Willingness to learn, adapt to changing operational requirements, and work in diverse environments
* Maintains composure in challenging or potentially confrontational situations
* Committed to working outside standard office hours when required

Job Description

**Research Assistant/Associate - Centre for Sustainable Medicine**
==================================================================

Job Title: Research Assistant/Associate - Centre for Sustainable Medicine

University-Level Unit: Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine

Faculty/Department-Level Unit: Dean-Med-Centre for Sustainable Medicine

Employee Category: Research Staff

Location\\_ONB: Kent Ridge Campus

Posting Start Date: 04/06/2026

**Job Description**
-------------------

Climate change is the defining challenge of this century, and healthcare is both a victim of climate change and a major contributor to it. The Centre for Sustainable Medicine (CoSM) at the National University of Singapore works at the frontier of policy, clinical systems, and global health to accelerate the transition to low-carbon, climate-resilient health systems across Asia and worldwide.

**Purpose of the Post**

We invite applications from a dynamic, experienced professional to help advance CoSM’s research priorities and to strengthen the real-world uptake of the Centre’s work.

The postholder will work across the Centre’s major workstreams - including health system carbon analytics, clinical transformation, and capacity building - ensuring that research and technical evidence are synthesised, interpreted, and translated into decision-ready outputs for policymakers, health system leaders, clinicians, partners, and other stakeholders.

This is a cross-cutting role at the interface of research, policy, and implementation. The successful candidate will play a leading role in converting evidence into high-impact products, supporting policy feedback cycles, and strengthening lessons from implementation and stakeholder engagement to inform the Centre’s future research.

**Key Responsibilities and Roles**
----------------------------------

* **Research synthesis, analysis, and translation**

* Contribute to the development of research outputs, including reports, peer-reviewed publications, technical analyses, and policy papers.
* Support the analysis and interpretation of research findings from CoSM projects, including emissions baselines, adaptation and mitigation strategies, health system analytics, and education initiatives.
* Translate research outputs into clear and actionable products for policy and practice, including policy briefs, executive summaries, technical guidance, and knowledge products.
* Identify cross-cutting insights from CoSM’s body of work and shape coherent evidence narratives that communicate the Centre’s contribution to global sustainable healthcare transformation.
* Support the preparation of academic publications, including drafting sections of manuscripts, coordinating co-author inputs, and assisting with reference management and editorial processes.
  

* **Policy feedback and implementation learning**

* Support the policy feedback cycle by gathering and synthesising insights from governments, delivery partners, clinicians, and other stakeholders on how evidence is being received, interpreted, and applied.
* Help ensure that lessons from implementation and engagement feed back into research framing, future analysis, and programme development.
* Facilitate structured dialogue between research teams and policy or practice stakeholders to strengthen the relevance, usability, and timing of CoSM outputs.
* Support the development and coordination of communities of practice across Asia-Pacific and globally, particularly in areas such as net zero healthcare, climate-resilient health systems, and health system decarbonisation.
  

* **Knowledge and evidence dissemination**

* Support dissemination of research through regional and global platforms, including technical forums, convenings, policy roundtables, and academic or professional events.
* Prepare high-quality briefing materials, concept notes, slide decks, summary papers, and dissemination products for international events, multilateral engagements, and senior partner discussions.
* Develop accessible summaries and tailored synthesis materials for different stakeholder groups, including ministries of health, hospital leaders, clinicians, finance stakeholders, academic audiences, and learners.
* Support the strategic positioning of CoSM’s flagship initiatives by ensuring clarity, consistency, and strong evidence-based narratives across written, digital, and presentation materials.

**Qualifications**
------------------

***Essential***

* A Bachelor’s degree or Master’s degree in public health, health policy, health systems, environmental health, economics, social policy, or a related field.
* 3-8 years of experience in research, public policy, evidence synthesis, policy-facing roles, or related functions.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret and translate complex technical or research material into clear, structured, and compelling outputs for varied audiences.
* Strong analytical and writing skills, with excellent editorial judgement and the ability to distil evidence without oversimplifying it.
* Experience working with multidisciplinary teams and engaging senior stakeholders across research, policy, and implementation settings.
* Strong organisational skills and ability to manage multiple workstreams simultaneously.
  

***Highly desirable***

* Experience working with governments, multilateral organisations, or large health systems.
* Familiarity with climate, sustainability, or health system transformation agendas.
* Experience working at the interface of research, policy, and implementation.
* Experience supporting dissemination of research through policy products, technical guidance, publications, or high-level stakeholder briefings.
* Experience supporting regional or international partnerships.
  

Remuneration will be commensurate with the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Informal enquiries are welcome and should be made to Jit Sohal, Head of Strategy and Impact, at joincosm@nus.edu.sg

  

**Formal application**: Please submit your application, indicating current/expected salary, supported by a detailed CV (including personal particulars, academic and employment history, complete list of publications/oral presentations (if any) and full contacts of three (3) referees to joincosm@nus.edu.sg. We regret that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

* Well-versed in topical knowledge of:

* Details of two referees (preferably academic) who can comment on the applicant’s academic abilities and research experience
  

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

You will provide strategic and hands-on leadership to strengthen a proactive safety culture, ensure regulatory and corporate compliance, and drive continuous improvement aligned with Emerson’s values of innovation, integrity, collaboration, and inclusion.

**In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Be:**

Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of HSE and sustainability programs to ensure a safe, healthy, and environmentally responsible workplace.  

Drive risk reduction initiatives to prevent injuries, incidents, and environmental impacts while protecting people, property, and the environment.  
* Monitor, analyze, and communicate HSE performance using leading and lagging indicators to support data-informed decision-making.
* Provide subject matter expertise and ownership for implementing tools, standards, training, and proven practices across the organization.
* Ensure ISO certification through effective audits and timely closure of corrective and preventive actions.
* Partner with leaders to embed HSE accountability and cultivate a positive, inclusive safety culture.
* Ensure new projects obtain all required HSE authorizations and permits prior to execution.
* Lead incident assessments, investigations, root cause validation, and corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
* Champion sustainability initiatives, including energy conservation, waste minimization, emissions reduction strategies, and progress toward Net Zero goals.

  + Represent Asia Pacific in global HSE meetings, translate global directives into regional actions, and collaborate closely with regional and country safety committees, business units, and leadership teams.
  + Harmonize and standardize Asia Pacific HSE processes, promoting collaboration and sharing of proven practices.
  Serve as Asia Pacific system administrator for HSE platforms (e.g. Velocity and Environment Health Safety (ENHESA) regulatory compliance, and risk management audit tools), mentoring key users and supporting inspections and audits across the Asia Pacific region.

You observe situational and group dynamics and select best-fit approaches. You are open to change and continue to learn and experience new opportunities. * Candidates with a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in Engineering / Safety Science / Occupational Health or related technical field will be considered.
* 7 or more years’ experience in HSE role.
* Practical knowledge of HSE regulatory compliance and industry trends.
* Knowledge of Country general safety policies and procedures.

Ability to influence and challenge current practices through process knowledge and personal relationships.

Our culture offers flexible time off plans, including paid parental leave (maternal and paternal), vacation and holiday leave.

The Financial Services Regulatory Authority is the financial services regulator in St Helena, a UK Overseas Territory. The FSRA wishes to appoint a suitably qualified individual to the position of **Implementation Manager - Regulatory Reform and Sustainable Finance** in a major regulatory and operational modernisation project.

The FSRA is leading a programme of work to transform St Helena into a new international financial hub, focused on sustainable finance. This transformation involves a complete modernisation of anti-money laundering legislation, company law, tax law and financial services regulation.

These regulatory and legal changes in turn need to be implemented at an organisational and institutional level.

**Purpose of the role**

You will work directly with the Asia-based CEO, and will:

* Act as the lead project manager for the implementation of the legislative and regulatory changes, by the FSRA, the St Helena Companies Registry and by local law enforcement bodies.
* Produce and keep up to date a detailed project plan and actions log for each legislative and regulatory workstream.
* Act as the lead project manager for the digitalization and overall operational transformation of the St Helena Companies Registry.
* Assist in developing our commercial strategy, including designing the “product” for our sustainable finance Company Registry and fund domicile.
* Assist in developing a tax strategy to support to support our sustainable finance and other commercial goals.
* Support the CEO, attending high-level meetings, taking ownership of follow-up actions and drafting executive briefings.
* Produce professional, corporate and investor presentations, to turn “dry” law into high-impact visual strategy for government officials and investors

**Candidate profile**

The successful candidate should have:

* Prior exposure to financial services regulation or company law, such as by working for a regulated firm in a compliance role, or as a regulator or in a professional services or audit firm.
* Prior experience in project management, involving implementation of legislative or regulatory change.
* Prior experience in projects involving operational and IT transformation.
* Strong and modern IT skills.
* Fluent English language skills.

The role might suit a recent graduate with a few years of work experience, or a later-career professional looking for a low stress role.

The role is offered as a 12-month fixed term contract, with the possibility of extension for a further 12-month period by mutual agreement. The role is offered on a 100% remote basis, with occasional in-person meetings with the CEO. For the right candidate, the role can be part-time.

The role reports to the head of the FSRA and it provides a great opportunity for a motivated individual to be part of a high-profile transformation programme.

Applications are invited by way of CV and covering letter and may be sent by email to info@fsra.sh
